- If sentiment is consistently positive (≥0.67) over recent days, model tends to overestimate prices; apply downward bias correction, especially after sharp spikes.
- If sentiment is negative (≤0.33) or mixed, model often underestimates; adjust upward, particularly if true outcome shows mean reversion or sudden drop.
- After a price spike (e.g., >83), model frequently overcorrects downward; reduce forecast slope for next 5–7 days to avoid overshoot.
- If true outcome shows strong mean reversion (e.g., 3–5 consecutive days falling from 80+), model often fails to recognize it; increase downward momentum in forecast.
- When sentiment shifts from positive to negative (or vice versa), model lags by 1–3 days; adjust forecast to reflect sentiment change 1–2 days ahead.
- For 30-day horizon, model often fails to capture early drop in sentiment-driven sell-off; add 1–2% downward adjustment if sentiment turns negative within 5 days.
- If recent history shows volatility >10% from mean, model tends to smooth too much; allow 3–5% volatility buffer in forecast for next 7 days.
